newsitem.title: JAPAN: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - May 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - May 8.

text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Japanese
press on Thursday, as reported by Kyodo news agency:
NIHON KEIZAI SHIMBUN:
-- Health insurance reform bill set to be passed by Lower
House on Thursday.
-- Finance Ministry to lift ban on brokerages from serving
concurrently as investment trust management firms and
investment advisory firms as early as April 1, 1998.
-- NEC Corp plans to launch semiconductor joint
venture in China.
-- Nissan Motor Co Ltd plans to set up new
decision-making system.
YOMIURI SHIMBUN:
-- Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) draft plan calls for drastic cut in education budget.
-- Two affiliates of religious group Ho-no-Hana Sampogyo fail to report 1.6 billion yen in taxable income.
-- Yomiuri Shimbun survey shows 16 of 71 garbage incinerators with excessive dioxin emissions to be scrapped or have their operations suspended.
ASAHI SHIMBUN:
-- Finance Ministry to review special deduction for insurance premiums, aiming at abolition or drastic cut in its 1998/99 tax reform plan.
-- Posts and Telecommunications Ministry to set new frequencies for radio communications to prevent helicopter accidents over disaster-hit areas.
-- Odawara city government to scrap academic record requirement for applicants for city jobs.
MAINICHI SHIMBUN:
-- Blue-ribbon panel on administrative reform to urge ministries and agencies to present own reform plans.
